facts.title: QR Code History
facts.content: QR codes were invented in 1994 by Denso Wave in Japan for tracking automotive parts in Toyota's manufacturing process.

facts.title: Scanning Distance
facts.content: For best results, hold your phone min 20-30 cms away from the QR code. Too close often causes focus issues!

facts.title: Storage Capacity
facts.content: A single QR code can store up to 3,000 alphanumeric characters - that's about half a page of text!

facts.title: Error Correction
facts.content: QR codes can still work perfectly even if up to 30% of the code is damaged, dirty, or artistically modified.

facts.title: Global Usage
facts.content: Over 11 million QR codes are scanned daily worldwide, making them one of the most used digital technologies.

facts.title: Art Integration
facts.content: Artistic QR codes maintain functionality while embedding logos, colors, and creative designs within the pattern.

facts.title: Speed Reading
facts.content: Modern smartphones can decode a QR code in less than 0.5 seconds using advanced computer vision algorithms.

facts.title: Future Tech
facts.content: QR codes are evolving with 3D versions, animated codes, and AI-enhanced designs for better user experiences.

facts.title: Moon Landing
facts.content: In 2019, SpaceIL's Beresheet lunar mission carried QR codes containing Wikipedia pages to the Moon - making them the first codes to leave Earth!

facts.title: Grave Memorials
facts.content: Some modern cemeteries use QR codes on tombstones that link to digital memorials, photos, and life stories of the deceased.

facts.title: Restaurant Revolution
facts.content: COVID-19 accelerated QR menu adoption by 750% - from novelty to necessity in just months, transforming the dining industry forever.

facts.title: Massive Scale
facts.content: The world's largest functional QR code covers 29,000 square meters in a Canadian corn maze - visible from aircraft and satellites!

facts.title: Wedding Innovation
facts.content: Modern couples embed QR codes in wedding invitations linking to photo albums, gift registries, and live ceremony streams for remote guests.

facts.title: Street Art Security
facts.content: Banksy and other artists hide QR codes in murals that authenticate artwork and link to exclusive content, fighting art forgery.

facts.title: Medical Lifesaver
facts.content: Emergency medical QR bracelets can instantly share critical health info, allergies, and emergency contacts with first responders.

facts.title: Time Capsule Tech
facts.content: The 2020 Tokyo Olympics buried QR codes in time capsules containing messages from athletes - to be opened in 2070!
